args.text: First look: a red popcorn machine in a big faint circle, 8 empty white dots above it, a coin counter at 0 on top, back/sound/restart buttons. A pointing finger icon sits on the machine - looks like it wants me to tap the machine. Bottom card shows a bucket, cost 25 coins, +10 -> +22 with an up arrow - an upgrade I can't afford yet (greyed). I expect tapping the machine pops popcorn, fills the 8 dots, and gives coins.

Each tap drops one kernel into a dot. After 8 taps the row emptied, popcorn flew out and I got 10 coins. The bottom card is now filling with yellow like a progress bar toward 25. So: 8 taps = one batch = +10. The upgrade turns a batch into +22. I need 3 batches. Tapping on.

30 coins now. The upgrade card turned bright yellow with a red arrow and red +22 - it's clearly saying 'buy me'. Tapping felt a bit slow and repetitive (taps each feel like a separate beat). Buying the bucket upgrade now.

Bought it! 30->5 coins. The machine grew bigger and got a striped awning with bunting - nice visible reward. Next upgrade is a cart for 64, +22 -> +48. Each batch should now pay 22. Let's see if that's true.
Yes: 5 + 22 = 27. The upgrade worked as advertised. Popcorn rains down more now. Curious whether holding my finger on the machine does something different (auto-pop?). Trying a 3-second hold.

Holding for 3 s only counted as one kernel - no auto-fill, no charge-up. So it's purely tap-tap-tap. A little disappointing; I hoped holding would do something. Will the machine do anything on its own if I wait? Waiting 10 s to check for idle income.

Nothing happens while idle - still 27, one kernel. The faint circle around the machine came back after I stopped tapping, like a 'tap here' reminder. So progress is 100% my taps. Next goal: 64 for the cart, about 2 more batches. Tapping again.
